Below is a quick‑look table of the **federal holidays that create long weekends in Canada for 2023**.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the following Monday is usually observed as a holiday, which also creates a long weekend.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Observed (if weekend) | Long‑Weekend Dates |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-----------------------|--------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 | Sunday | Jan 2 (Mon) | Jan 1–3 |
| Family Day (BC, AB, ON, SK, NB, PE) | Feb 20 | Monday | — | Feb 18–20 |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Friday | — | Apr 7–9 |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Monday | — | May 20–22 |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 | Saturday | Jul 3 (Mon) | Jul 1–3 |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Monday | — | Sep 2–4 |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Monday | — | Oct 7–9 |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 | Saturday | Nov 13 (Mon) | Nov 11–13 |
| Christmas | Dec 25 | Monday | — | Dec 23–25 |

> **Note:**  
> • Provincial holidays (e.g., Family Day, St. Patrick’s Day, etc.) vary by province and may add additional long weekends.  
> • If you need the exact dates for a specific province, let me know and I can tailor the list accordingly.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app. If you’d like to programmatically calculate the number of days between two dates (e.g., to determine how many days you’ll have off), you can use the `add` function below:

```json
{
  "functions.add": {
    "a": 5,
    "b": 3
  }
}
```

(Replace `a` and `b` with the number of days you want to add.)
